about: ICF's member standards and every Standards Committee ballot on them, 2019 on (VAULT-DESIGN §5.4). Hand-written; scripts/build-elections-plan.mjs turns each ballot into a standards-ballot election. An item with fail: true must fail two-thirds of votes cast; a recirculation (round > 0) follows its prior ballot on the same document, and carry names the prior item whose unsatisfied disapprovers vote against again. dis is the share of votes cast that disapprove; gist is what the section says, for the comment writer.

ICF-STD-101.title: Code of Practice for Raw-Milk Cheese Aging

ICF-STD-201.title: Labeling Guide for Aged and Washed-Rind Cheeses

items.name: §1 Scope and definitions
items.gist: Covers cheese made from unpasteurized milk by ICF member producers, and defines make date, aging and release.

items.name: §2 Minimum aging before sale
items.gist: Raw-milk cheese is held at least 60 days at 35°F (1.7°C) or above from the make date before it is sold, matching the federal floor.

items.name: §3 Aging-room conditions
items.gist: Temperature and humidity are logged at least daily in every room that holds raw-milk cheese; rooms are cleaned on a written schedule.

items.name: §4 Release checks
items.gist: Before release each batch is checked against its make record and aging log; a batch with a gap in its log is held until reviewed.

items.name: §1 Herd health and milking hygiene
items.gist: A written herd-health plan reviewed with a veterinarian each year; teat preparation and pre-dip before every milking.

items.name: §2 Bulk-tank testing
items.gist: Draft: every herd tests its bulk-tank milk for standard plate count and coliforms every week. Small and seasonal herds say weekly lab testing is costly and their nearest lab is far away.

items.name: §3 Milk holding and transport
items.gist: Raw milk for cheese is cooled to 40°F (4.4°C) or below within two hours of milking, or used within the hour.

items.name: §2 Bulk-tank testing (revised)
items.gist: Revised after the first ballot: weekly testing in the first eight weeks of each milking season and every second week after that; herds under 40 head may test a pooled sample.

items.name: §1 What to record for each batch
items.gist: Make date, milk source, culture lot, salting, each move between rooms, and the release date.

items.name: §2 Keeping records
items.gist: Records are kept for at least two years after the last wheel of a batch is sold, on paper or electronically.

items.name: §3 Cheese aged by someone else
items.gist: When an affineur or another member ages the cheese, the maker keeps a copy of the aging log for each batch.

items.name: Amendment 1: cheese aged off-site
items.gist: Adds to §2 that the 60-day period runs across moves between sites, provided the receiving site keeps the same daily log.

items.name: §1 Category names
items.gist: Members use the ICF category names on labels: fresh, bloomy-rind, washed-rind, natural-rind and hard aged.

items.name: §2 Washed-rind definition
items.gist: Draft: a cheese may be labeled washed-rind only if its rind is washed with brine at least twice a week throughout aging. Makers who wash with beer, wine or spirits, or who wash only early in aging, say the draft shuts them out.

items.name: §3 Age statements
items.gist: An age statement on a label gives the minimum age of the wheels in the lot, in days or months.

items.name: §4 Raw-milk disclosure
items.gist: Labels on raw-milk cheese say 'made with raw milk' on the front panel.

items.name: §2 Washed-rind definition (revised)
items.gist: Revised: the rind is washed or smeared with a brine, beer, wine or spirit solution, repeatedly during at least the first half of aging.

items.name: §1 Net weight on whole wheels
items.gist: Whole wheels are labeled with their net weight at packing, excluding wax and wrapping.

items.name: §2 Cut-and-wrap wedges
items.gist: Wedges cut at retail are weighed and labeled at the counter after wrapping, less the tare of the wrap.

items.name: §3 Moisture loss
items.gist: Producers tell buyers the expected moisture loss for each style, so retailers can reweigh older stock.

items.name: Amendment 1: small and seasonal herds
items.gist: Adds a short guide for herds under 40 head: the pooled sample, a list of approved labs, and what to do after a high count.

items.name: Amendment 1: electronic records and sensor logs
items.gist: Data-logger and sensor exports count as the aging log if they are kept unedited and can be printed on request.

items.name: §1 Scope and definitions (revised)
items.gist: Adds washed-curd and stretched-curd styles, and points to ICF-STD-102 for records.

items.name: §2 Minimum aging before sale
items.gist: Unchanged: at least 60 days at 35°F (1.7°C) or above from the make date.

items.name: §3 Validated aging protocols
items.gist: New draft: each member producer writes down and validates its own aging protocol for each raw-milk style, beyond the federal minimum, and has it reviewed by an outside expert every three years. Smaller makers say an outside review every three years is costly; some ask for peer review instead.

items.name: §4 Release checks (revised)
items.gist: Adds a hold-and-test step for any batch whose aging log shows a temperature excursion.

items.name: §5 Aging records
items.gist: Replaces the old record clauses with a reference to ICF-STD-102.

items.name: §3 Validated aging protocols (revision 1)
items.gist: Revised: the written protocol is validated once, then reviewed every three years by an outside expert or by two peer reviewers from an ICF list. Opponents still object that the peer route has no conflict-of-interest rule and that the first validation is due within a year.

items.name: §3 Validated aging protocols (revision 2)
items.gist: Revised again: adds a conflict-of-interest rule for peer reviewers, gives producers two years to validate their first protocol, and lets one validation cover close variants of a style.

items.name: §1 Monitoring points
items.gist: Each aging room has a written map of sampling points: shelves, floor drains, walls and air handlers.

items.name: §2 Sampling frequency
items.gist: Environmental swabs at least monthly in every room, and weekly in rooms holding raw-milk soft cheese.

items.name: §3 Corrective action
items.gist: A positive swab triggers cleaning, resampling, and a hold on product from that room until a resample is clear.

items.name: Amendment 1: age statements on mixed lots
items.gist: When a lot mixes wheels of different ages, the age statement gives the age of the youngest wheel.

items.name: §A1 Scope
items.gist: Applies ICF-STD-101 to cheese made from sheep or goat milk, and from mixed milks.

items.name: §A2 Aging periods for sheep and goat milk
items.gist: Draft: raw-milk cheese from sheep or goat milk is aged at least 90 days, beyond the 60-day floor. Sheep and goat dairies say the evidence for 90 days is thin and their milking seasons are short.

items.name: §A3 Seasonal milk supply
items.gist: Allows frozen sheep-milk curd to be used, with its freeze date in the make record.

items.name: §A2 Aging periods for sheep and goat milk (revised)
items.gist: Revised: the 60-day floor applies; a longer period is recommended, not required, for soft and semi-soft styles, with each maker's reasons recorded in its validated protocol under ICF-STD-101 §3.

items.name: §1 Net weight on whole wheels
items.gist: Unchanged from 1.0: net weight at packing, excluding wax and wrapping.

items.name: §2 Cut-and-wrap wedges (revised)
items.gist: Lets retailers use a printed tare for each type of wrap instead of weighing the wrap each time.

items.name: §3 Moisture-loss allowance
items.gist: Producers publish a moisture-loss allowance for each style, as a percentage per month of age.

items.name: §4 Shipped and online orders
items.gist: New: an online listing states the net weight at packing and that weight may fall slightly in transit.
